description: Keystroke latency gate config. On pull_request CI runs we collect alternating base/HEAD benchmark rounds on the SAME runner, then compare the median round-level metric for each revision. This cancels runner speed and reduces order effects. Relative p50 is the merge gate; p99 is retained as an advisory until each benchmark run has enough observations to make p99 stable. Absolute ceilings remain catastrophic sanity bounds.

relative._note: HEAD <= base * (1 + pct/100), evaluated from the median of repeated same-runner round metrics. p50 +10% is merge-blocking. p99 +20% is reported but non-blocking because 120 observations per run is not enough for a stable 99th-percentile gate. Both still use absolute sanity bounds.

absolute_sanity._note: Loose CATASTROPHIC sanity bounds only. They complement the strict relative p50 gate and remain the only blocking p99 bound while relative p99 is advisory. They are deliberately generous so a healthy runner never trips them (p50 4000us is ~2.2x the ~1800us M1 baseline and ~2.4x a fast 1694us runner read). They catch a ~2x regression even when the base benchmark is unavailable. Recalibrate only if normal runner reads start approaching these numbers.

ratchet: Ratchet protocol: after each fast-path optimization PR merges (#2287, #2288, #2289), tighten the p50 relative tolerance toward 0 as the alternating-round spread shrinks. Promote p99 from advisory to a merge gate only after increasing per-run observations enough to make its estimate stable at practical CI runtime. Lower absolute_sanity bounds only toward (new typical runner read + generous margin); never below ~2x a healthy runner read.
